newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu says Hebron summit with Arafat not set.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu says Hebron summit with Arafat not set.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Wednesday that he and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat had yet to schedule a summit to sew up a deal giving self-rule to the last West Arab Bank town of Hebron.

Asked at Israel's parliament whether he would meet Arafat on Wednesday, Netanyahu said: "Possibly. We will see later. We haven't yet scheduled a meeting...We're still in the final steps of the conclusion of the Hebron negotiations."
"When I am satisfied that the basic conditions of security will have been reached, then we will sign it," Netanyahu told Israel Radio's English news.

Despite his opposition -- and that of right-wing cabinet members -- to swapping occupied Arab land for peace, Netanyahu came to power on a promise to uphold the peace deals with the PLO of the left-leaning government he ousted in May.
"Cabinet ministers can vote as they wish but I think that we have a responsibility and I am confident that we'll pass it in the cabinet," Netanyahu said.

"It was a very bad agreement that we received from the previous government but I think it's been vastly improved," he said of the accord which will give Arafat's Palestinian Authority control of most of the West Bank town where 400 Jews live and study in the heart of 100,000 Arabs.
